name: NLC India Ltd
tagline: Navratna PSU lignite-miner-cum-thermal-power generator executing a concrete renewable pivot (10 GW target by 2030, renewable capacity already ~1.4 GW and rising, NIRL green-energy arm hiving off assets and just forming a new JV with PTC India, IPO in the works) - FY26 revenue grew ~14% and PAT +39% YoY, so the pivot is now showing up in delivered numbers, not just guidance. Still, at ~Rs 37,250 Cr market cap and PSU-utility ROCE (~8%), size and structure rule out an extreme-return thesis; the stock currently trades near brokerages' bear-case price, which is the main reason for interest.
business_overview: NLC India Ltd (formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation) mines lignite/coal and operates thermal power plants (7,694 MW installed incl. JVs across 6 mines and 17 power plants in 11 states), and is explicitly pivoting toward renewables via its subsidiary NIRL (NLC India Renewables Ltd): renewable capacity has grown from 734 MW to roughly 1.4 GW operational (303 MW added in FY26 alone) against a stated 10 GW-by-2030 target, with a further ~5.8 GW pipeline/under-implementation and ~2.5 GW under construction. NLC hived off 708.96 MW of renewable assets (incl. a 4 MW green hydrogen pilot) to NIRL, and on 16-Sep-2026 NIRL and PTC India incorporated a joint venture, 'NIRL PTC Renewables Ltd', for further green-energy project development - a fresh, dated step taken just two days before this review. NIRL is targeting an IPO (~Rs 4,000 Cr raise) to fund the renewable scale-up; the exact filing/listing window has been reported inconsistently across sources (as early as Q4 FY26/Q1 FY27, as late as Q2 FY27) and no confirmed DRHP filing was found this pass, so treat the timeline as soft/slipping. On the core business, Ghatampur Thermal Unit III was commissioned (~June 2026, full-year FY27 contribution still ramping) and the Pachwara South coal block began mining in March 2026 (peak capacity 9 MTPA), improving fuel security. Confirmed as the exact listed entity matching state.json name via screener.in/tickertape (NSE: NLCINDIA). Seeded via untrusted X triage (@StocksResearch, 2026-09-13, high conviction).

fundamentals_narrative: Fresh filings correct the prior pass's 'flat revenue' read: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 14.4% YoY to Rs 17,490cr and PAT rose 38.9% to a record Rs 3,769cr, with Q1 FY27 revenue up a further 23% YoY - the renewable/thermal capacity build-out is now showing up in delivered numbers, not just guidance. Returns remain modest for the capital deployed (ROCE ~7.7-8%, never crossing 15% in the last 5 FYs) and leverage is rising (D/E ~1.3x, up from 0.47x in FY15) as capex stays heavy (~Rs 9,131cr in FY26) across Ghatampur thermal, Pachwara coal and the NIRL renewable build. The renewable pivot itself has become more concrete since the last look: capacity has nearly doubled to ~1.4 GW, 708.96 MW of assets have been hived off into NIRL, and NIRL just formed a fresh JV with PTC India (16-Sep-2026, two days before this review) - continued momentum, not a stalled story. Valuation is undemanding and arguably interesting: the current price (~Rs 269) sits almost exactly at brokerages' bear-case scenario (~Rs 270) despite FY26 numbers beating and the renewable story advancing, versus a base case near Rs 400 (Axis Securities target Rs 385). Set against that: the NIRL IPO timeline has been reported inconsistently across sources and shows signs of slipping, a brand-new CMD (Dr. Prasanna Kumar Acharya, effective 17-Sep-2026 - literally the day before this review) has just taken over, and Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT fell 39% YoY on a high prior-year exceptional-item base despite strong revenue/EBITDA growth.

value_chain.theme: Indian power generation - captive-lignite/coal thermal PSU pivoting into utility-scale renewables (solar/wind/BESS/pumped-storage/green hydrogen)
value_chain.position: Vertically integrated captive-lignite miner + thermal genco (6 mines, 17 plants, 7,694 MW incl. JVs), now building a separate renewable-generation arm (NIRL, ~1.4 GW) via organic capacity additions plus a new JV with PTC India for project development/offtake

value_chain.note: Core lignite/thermal book is a captive, low-competition franchise (real moat there), but the renewable pivot places NLC into a competitively-bid, capital-intensive segment shared with NTPC Green, SJVN and Adani Green. NLC's edge is government-backed land/financing access and its new PTC India JV for trading/offtake, not a technology or cost moat - consistent with the 'moat: weak' four_box call.

management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit, named move from pure lignite-mining/thermal-generation into a diversified energy platform - renewables, a green hydrogen pilot, BESS, pumped-storage hydro, lignite-to-methanol, and critical-mineral exploration (phosphorite/limestone licenses secured) - a genuine stated value-chain broadening, not just marketing language.

Expected for a capital-intensive, regulated-return PSU utility; it does not by itself argue against the renewable-pivot thesis, but it confirms this is a re-rating/pivot story rather than a Coffee-Can compounder.
